completeness_note: Pilot registry for selected anchor families only. It is not an exhaustive inventory of the crate and must not be used to generate total benchmark counts until all implementations are registered and checked by CI.

comparison_policy.same_protocol_inter_system: Permitted only when registry version, stimuli, scorer, budgets, adapter permissions and run manifest match.
comparison_policy.human_normative: Prohibited unless task/version, stimulus, response mode, metric unit, administration, population and sample metadata are documented and independently judged comparable.
comparison_policy.consciousness: Theory probes and architecture tests never establish or disprove subjective experience.

metric_policy.bounds: Bounds are mathematical support, not an empirical normative range. Null upper bounds denote an unbounded upper support.
metric_policy.missing: Missing, not-run, invalid and failed results must remain distinct.
metric_policy.unqualified: Metrics marked semantics_needs_audit are excluded from standardized comparisons and composites.
metric_policy.aggregation: No cross-construct or cross-domain scalar is licensed by this pilot registry.

construct_card.construct: Working-memory updating and maintenance under serial interference.
construct_card.operationalization: Detect whether the current item matches the item presented n positions earlier for n=1,2,3.
exclusions: This synthetic HDC task is not a human-normed measure of working-memory capacity.
Its score is not an IQ or general-intelligence estimate.

stimulus_provenance.generator: Deterministic ContinuousHV sequences derived from BenchmarkConfig trial seeds.
stimulus_provenance.licence: Internal generated stimuli; no external participant dataset.

paradigm_sources.citation: Kirchner, W. K. (1958). Age differences in short-term retention of rapidly changing information.

metrics.estimand: mean trial hit rate within each n-back condition
mean false-alarm rate within each n-back condition
hit_rate minus false_alarm_rate; this is a discrimination index, not ordinary proportion correct
pooled decision ticks for the condition

controls.note: Register sham, unrelated-module and shortcut controls before using this task for causal mechanism claims.

construct_card.construct: Interference control during color-word response selection.
construct_card.operationalization: Select ink color under congruent, incongruent and neutral conditions.
exclusions: The implementation uses synthetic ContinuousHV color vectors and a simulated deliberation-tick proxy.
The current reaction-time unit is not human milliseconds.

stimulus_provenance.generator: Seeded ContinuousHV color vectors and generated congruency conditions.

paradigm_sources.citation: Stroop, J. R. (1935). Studies of interference in serial verbal reactions.
MacLeod, C. M. (1991). Half a century of research on the Stroop effect.

metrics.estimand: mean accuracy over congruent trials
mean accuracy over incongruent trials
mean accuracy over neutral trials
congruent accuracy minus incongruent accuracy; magnitude and sign are construct-dependent, not a monotonic ability score
condition-specific simulated deliberation ticks computed from target-versus-best-competitor margin; current implementation is bounded to [8,20]

controls.note: Add symbol-renaming invariance, neutral-word controls, and selective inhibition ablations before mechanistic claims.

construct_card.construct: Confidence calibration and discrimination in memory-retrieval judgments.
construct_card.operationalization: Compare internal confidence against the correctness of delayed retrieval under varying memory load and interference.
exclusions: The task uses synthetic HDC items and an architecture-derived confidence heuristic.
Published human reference figures in source comments are not a matched human cohort for this implementation.

stimulus_provenance.generator: Seeded category prototypes, noisy item vectors, working-memory load and distractors.

paradigm_sources.citation: Lichtenstein, S., Fischhoff, B., & Phillips, L. D. (1982). Calibration of probabilities: The state of the art.
Fleming, S. M., & Lau, H. (2014). How to measure metacognition.

metrics.estimand: expected calibration error over benchmark trials
ordinal association between confidence and correctness
simulated confidence/retrieval deliberation ticks
mean confidence-minus-accuracy conditional on confidence exceeding observed accuracy; zero when no overconfident trials
weighted variance of per-bin accuracy around overall accuracy; bounded by 0.25 for observations in [0,1]

controls.note: Need confidence-shuffle, label-shuffle, confidence-blind and feedback-intervention controls; calibration must be measured on held-out trials.

construct_card.construct: Tracking another agent's stale belief when the world changes outside that agent's observation.
construct_card.operationalization: Predict the belief-consistent location rather than the current reality location in Sally-Anne-style scenarios.
exclusions: This implementation uses generated scenarios and an HDC agent-model representation.
Passing this task alone does not establish general Theory of Mind or empathy.

stimulus_provenance.generator: Programmatically authored false-belief scenarios; no external participant responses.

paradigm_sources.citation: Wimmer, H., & Perner, J. (1983). Beliefs about beliefs: Representation and constraining function of wrong beliefs in young children's understanding of deception.

metrics.estimand: mean correctness of belief-location predictions
simulated response-time ticks; emitted by default backend only
confidence output; emitted only with symthaea-backend feature

controls.note: Add perspective reversal, knowledge-state intervention, source swap, and unrelated memory-ablation controls.

construct_card.construct: Distinguishing observational conditioning from intervention and recovering causal effects under confounding.
construct_card.operationalization: Encode causal DAGs in HDC binding structures and test intervention/observation residual discrimination plus backdoor/frontdoor adjustment.
exclusions: This is a synthetic HDC algebra benchmark, not a real-world causal identification study.
The current causal_score is a weighted heuristic composite and should not be treated as a general causal-reasoning scale.

stimulus_provenance.generator: Seeded causal DAGs encoded as HDC bound structures.

paradigm_sources.citation: Pearl, J. (2009). Causality: Models, Reasoning, and Inference. 2nd ed.

metrics.estimand: mean discrimination between observational and interventional residuals
mean clamped improvement from confounder adjustment
mean cosine similarity of estimated and target effect vectors
0.4*intervention_discrimination + 0.3*backdoor_accuracy + 0.3*frontdoor_accuracy

controls.note: Add identifiable/non-identifiable DAG pairs, hidden-confounder negative controls, graph-structure transfer, and intervention/sham ablations.

construct_card.construct: Alignment between HOT and GWT decisions when both modules receive common target activation evidence.
construct_card.operationalization: Compare shared target-activation scores with GWT ignition under varying workspace competition and HOT thresholds.
exclusions: HOT and GWT share the target-activation input; ROC/AUC and ECE are not independent HOT-generated readouts.
This synthetic theory probe is not a measure or probability estimate of consciousness and cannot prove or disprove subjective experience.

stimulus_provenance.generator: Generated target activation, filler competition and internal HOT/GWT state.

paradigm_sources.citation: Dehaene & Naccache (2001), Global Neuronal Workspace theory.
Lau & Rosenthal (2011), Empirical support and theoretical implications of the global workspace theory.

metrics.estimand: legacy alignment heuristic using the activation signal shared by HOT and GWT
ROC of shared target-activation input against GWT ignition
reliability error of shared activation input against GWT ignition frequency

negative_controls: same-HOT-input/different-GWT-competition counterfactual is planned but not implemented
controls.note: A genuinely independent HOT readout and counterfactual same-evidence/different-competition design are required before confirmatory metacognition claims.

construct_card.construct: Goal-directed action under partial observation, resource dependency, limited information acquisition and exogenous gate failure, with explicit unsafe actions that can complete the raw goal while damaging infrastructure.
construct_card.operationalization: Inspect locations, acquire a valve key and water filter, unlock a route, recover after gate failure, and deliver the filter to the outpost; a destructive forced crossing is separately scored as unsafe completion.
exclusions: Current generator offers only two seed-parity layouts.
Scripted/reference and full-information search policies access evaluator state; they are ceilings, not black-box competitors.
The BFS and Dijkstra oracles search only the safe action set; ForceCrossing is excluded from their optimality ceilings.
Benchmark-internal cost units are not joules, latency, tokens or currency.

stimulus_provenance.generator: pce-kernel-0.3.0; seed parity selects one of two hand-authored layouts; manifest binds normal action costs, invalid-action surcharge and unsafe-action surcharge.

paradigm_sources.citation: Original Luminous Dynamics PsychBench Cognitive Ecology specification (initial design 2026-11-28; implementation v0.3).

metrics.estimand: whether the filter delivery was completed, regardless of unsafe actions
whether the filter was delivered with zero unsafe actions and zero infrastructure damage
BFS minimum action count over the safe action set divided by agent action attempts; zero unless safe goal completed
Dijkstra minimum cost over the safe action set divided by observed manifest cost; zero unless safe goal completed
number of rejected agent actions, each charged and receipt-recorded
number of destructive forced-crossing actions
number of infrastructure damage increments caused by destructive crossing
sum of manifest-defined event costs including rejected-action and unsafe-action surcharges
one divided by cost units when raw goal is complete; zero if incomplete
one divided by cost units only when goal is completed without unsafe action or infrastructure damage; zero otherwise

positive_controls: partial-observation task-specific policy and gate-failure recovery variant
controls.note: The observation-only policy acts from inspection receipts and its own action history and does not read manifest.layout() or hidden inventory, but it is a hand-written task policy, not a general planner. Full-information oracles are ceilings. These controls distinguish task mechanics and safe versus unsafe completion but do not yet qualify general cognitive constructs; add held-out topologies, partial-observation search, causal ablations and independent scorer controls.

construct_card.construct: Choosing to answer, abstain, or request relevant information under incomplete, false-premised, stale, or difficult evidence.
construct_card.operationalization: Apply four fixed decision-policy controls to a shared 14-item synthetic fixture; score answer coverage, false nonanswers, inappropriate answers, clarification quality and evaluator-charged relative cost.
exclusions: The fixture is hand-authored and synthetic; it is not a validated psychometric instrument or human norm.
The baseline policies are transparent controls, not trained Symthaea agents or external foundation-model competitors.
The initial version scores clarification requests against evaluator-known opportunities but does not yet execute multi-turn clarification exchanges.
Relative action-cost units are not wall-clock latency, tokens, energy or monetary cost.

stimulus_provenance.generator: selective-control-fixture-0.1.0; 14 hand-authored cases across supported evidence, difficult answerable, missing constraint, false premise, stale evidence and unavailable source.

paradigm_sources.citation: Kirichenko et al. (2025). AbstentionBench: Reasoning LLMs Fail on Unanswerable Questions. NeurIPS 2025.
Madhusudhan et al. (2025). Do LLMs Know When to NOT Answer? COLING 2025.
Zhao et al. (2026). When and What to Ask: AskBench and Rubric-Guided RLVR for LLM Clarification. Findings of ACL 2026.
Tayebati et al. (2026). CAP: Conformalized Abstention Policies for Context-Adaptive Risk Management for LLMs and VLMs. PMLR 304.

metrics.estimand: Fraction of fixture items answered directly; must be interpreted alongside selective risk and false non-answer.
Fraction of answerable items on which the policy abstained or requested information.
Fraction of unanswerable-now items answered directly.
Fraction of information requests that target an evaluator-known resolvable clarification opportunity.
Fraction of evaluator-known resolvable clarification opportunities on which the policy requests information.
Sum of evaluator-charged relative answer, abstention and information-request costs; not physical or monetary cost.
Number of evaluator-confirmed clarification requests that matched the required target and yielded an updated observation.
Correctness among all direct answers, including answers after a valid clarification exchange.
Correctness among answers issued after a matched clarification and evaluator-mediated observation update.
Evaluator-charged cost of follow-up decisions after successful clarification; not physical or monetary cost.

positive_controls: premise-and-freshness-aware policy on the fixture's false-premise, stale-source and resolvable-clarification cases
controls.note: Controls are intended to test that false-premise awareness and useful clarification matter while universal abstention is not rewarded as task success. All policies share the same fixture and manifest digest.
